correctness.rationale: Anchoring the apex at zero gives |x_i|<=1 and adjacent rim jumps <=1. The variance Hessian is positive definite on anchored vectors; thus each maximizer is extreme. A common small perturbation of any tight-edge component at noninteger values contradicts extremality; every maximum uses {-1,0,1}. Writing a,b,z for the two signed counts and zeros gives exactly N^2 Var=N(a+b)-(a-b)^2. Opposite signs require one separator zero on paths or two on cycles; balanced counts maximize this expression, while extra zeros or one-sign competitors are inferior. This proves formulas and all equality profiles for all m, not an enumeration extrapolation. Independent brute exact-fraction enumeration on 3<=m<=8 recovered the maxima and parity counts, including 14/25 for F4 and 2/5 for W4.

value.rationale: Quantifies the exact variance cost of adding one edge between the ends of a path joined to a universal apex. This edge perturbation makes a global Lipschitz optimization comparison of two standard diameter-two graph families; the parity-dependent 1/N penalty, sharp value and all optimizers are natural independently usable invariants beyond generic integrality.

final_claim: For all integers m>=4, the uniform-vertex unit-Lipschitz spread on fan K_1 join P_m is (m-1)/(m+1)-epsilon_(m-1)/(m+1)^2 and on wheel K_1 join C_m is (m-2)/(m+1)-epsilon_(m-2)/(m+1)^2; the edge-closing penalty is ((m+1)-(-1)^m)/(m+1)^2, with complete apex-anchored equality classification.
limitations: All vertices count equally; all edges unit; m>=4 for comparison; no arbitrary rim weights.
Independent finite enumeration checks only m<=8; infinite proof is the symbolic tight-component and signed-count argument.
